note.explanation: The modern periodic table arranges elements by increasing atomic number. Elements are placed in horizontal periods and vertical groups. Elements in the same group have similar outermost-shell electronic configurations and therefore similar chemical properties.
examples: Sodium and chlorine are placed in the same period because they are in the same horizontal row.
Elements in one vertical column belong to the same group.
note.checkAnswer: The horizontal rows are periods, and the vertical columns are groups.
note.simple: Think of the periodic table as a chart: elements go from left to right in increasing atomic number, and elements with similar properties are placed in the same vertical column.
note.checkQuestion: What are the horizontal rows and vertical columns of the periodic table called?
note.title: How the Modern Periodic Table Is Arranged
steps: Arrange the elements in ascending order of atomic number.
Read across each horizontal row, called a period.
Read down each vertical column, called a group.
Notice that properties repeat at regular intervals and that elements in a group have similar chemical properties.
note.answer: The modern periodic table arranges elements in increasing atomic number, in periods and groups.

explain.title: The modern table is arranged by atomic number
explain.body: The modern periodic table is based upon the arrangement of elements according to increasing atomic number. Elements are arranged from left to right in ascending order of their atomic numbers.

explain.title: Periods and groups
explain.body: The horizontal rows of elements in the periodic table are called periods while the vertical columns are called groups.

explain.title: Why properties repeat
explain.body: In a period, electronic configuration changes from left to right, so properties change gradually. Elements in a group have similar electronic configurations in their outermost shells and show similar chemical properties. Properties repeat after regular intervals; this trend is called periodicity in the properties.

mistakes: Do not confuse periods and groups: periods are horizontal rows, while groups are vertical columns.
Do not say the modern periodic table is arranged by atomic mass; it is arranged by increasing atomic number.
Do not claim that elements in a group have identical properties; say that they show similar chemical properties.
Do not forget to explain that periodicity means properties repeat after regular intervals.
